metadata.name: OWASP Top 10 Detection Rules
metadata.description: Detection rules derived from OWASP Top 10 2021 for Python source code analysis.

rules.description: MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken hash functions. OWASP A02:2021 prohibits use of weak or deprecated cryptographic algorithms.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512. Example: hashlib.sha256(data)

rules.description: Importing MD5 or SHA-1 from PyCrypto/PyCryptodome indicates use of broken hash functions. OWASP A02:2021 requires strong, approved algorithms.
rules.remediation: Use SHA-256 or SHA-3: from Crypto.Hash import SHA256

rules.description: DES (Data Encryption Standard) is a broken symmetric cipher. OWASP A02:2021 prohibits weak encryption algorithms that are known to be insecure.
rules.remediation: Use AES-256 with GCM mode: from Crypto.Cipher import AES; AES.new(key, AES.MODE_GCM)

rules.description: DES cipher imported from PyCrypto/PyCryptodome. DES is a broken algorithm. OWASP A02:2021 requires the use of strong, modern encryption.
rules.remediation: Replace with AES: from Crypto.Cipher import AES

rules.description: AES ECB mode encrypts identical plaintext blocks into identical ciphertext blocks, revealing data patterns. OWASP A02:2021 requires semantically secure cipher modes.
rules.remediation: Use AES.MODE_GCM (authenticated) or AES.MODE_CBC with a random IV.

rules.description: Python's random.random() uses the Mersenne Twister PRNG which is not cryptographically secure. OWASP A02:2021 requires cryptographically strong random number generation.
rules.remediation: Use the secrets module: import secrets; secrets.token_bytes(32)

rules.description: random.randint() is not cryptographically secure. OWASP A02:2021 requires use of cryptographically strong random generators for security-sensitive operations.
RSA keys shorter than 2048 bits are vulnerable to factorization attacks. OWASP A02:2021 requires adequate encryption strength.
rules.remediation: Use RSA.generate(2048) or higher. RSA.generate(4096) recommended for long-term security.

rules.description: Hardcoded credentials in source code are exposed to anyone with code access. OWASP A07:2021 identifies hardcoded passwords as a critical authentication failure.
rules.remediation: Store secrets in environment variables: os.environ.get('SECRET_KEY') or use a secrets manager.

rules.description: SECRET_KEY is hardcoded in source code. This is a critical security risk exposing cryptographic keys. OWASP A07:2021 prohibits hardcoded authentication credentials.
Disabling TLS certificate verification allows man-in-the-middle attacks. OWASP A02:2021 requires proper certificate validation for all encrypted communications.
RC4, RC2, and Blowfish are weak ciphers not recommended for use. OWASP A02:2021 requires strong, modern encryption algorithms.
rules.remediation: Use AES-256 with GCM mode for authenticated encryption.
